back: Global Positioning System: a receiver calculates its exact position from the signals of several satellites.
GPS receiver in each vehicle sends its position over the mobile network to a central computer that shows vehicles on a map.
Induction loops and cameras count vehicles; the computer adjusts traffic light timings to reduce queues.
A patient's medical history stored on a computer system for authorised staff to access and share.
Sensors measure vital signs continuously; the computer compares readings with safe limits, displays them and sounds an alarm when outside.
Collecting data automatically from sensors at set intervals and storing it for later analysis.
Weather stations, pollution sensors, satellite images and GIS, flood and fire early-warning systems.
Patient data is sensitive: it must be protected from hackers and unauthorised staff.
